By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 25, 2026 at 7:12PM EST Key Points Vertex's cystic fibrosis monopoly, protected into the late 2030s, still drives consistent revenue and earnings growth. The company’s efforts to diversify its lineup should pay rich dividends down the road. 10 stocks we like better than Vertex Pharmaceuticals › Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX +0.04%), a biotech company, has been on an impressive run over the past decade. If you had invested $10,000 in the stock in 2016, you'd have about $61,660 today. By comparison, $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 10 years ago would be worth about $38,663 today (with dividends reinvested) -- that's not bad, but it pales in comparison to the returns you would have had with Vertex. That said, the past is the past. The important question is whether the drugmaker can deliver similarly impressive returns going forward. Image source: The Motley Fool. Entering a new era Vertex has crushed broader equity markets thanks to its dominance in the cystic fibrosis (CF) market. The company has very little competition in this niche, and thanks to several new launches over the past 10 years that have allowed it to treat increasingly more CF patients, revenue and earnings growth have been strong. Vertex's CF franchise should remain an important growth driver over the next decade. After all, the company's most important medicines won't lose patent exclusivity until the late 2030s. But in the meantime, Vertex should significantly diversify and expand its lineup. The company's work in kidney diseases looks particularly promising. Vertex Pharmaceuticals could earn approval for one product in its kidney disease portfolio, povetacicept -- a medicine for IgA nephropathy -- by the end of the month. This medicine has peak sales potential of around $4 billion across IgA nephropathy and other potential indications, according to some estimates.
